method: Source inventory, project documentation, and targeted application code review. Runtime tests were not run across the other companies. This is a dated review snapshot, not a live repository connection.

entries.name: Resume Layout Studio
entries.title: Make one saved-resume route require a verified session
entries.finding: Local accounts and saved resumes use browser storage; the first local account becomes admin.
entries.action: Create a backend session check for the saved-resume read route and stop accepting a client-selected account as authorization. Keep a clearly labelled local demo mode.
entries.acceptance: An unauthenticated request is rejected, account A cannot read account B, and the normal resume preview still works.

entries.name: Pre-loved by Lhota
entries.title: Verify stock cannot be oversold by concurrent checkouts
entries.finding: The storefront has checkout, inventory updates, and order creation paths.
entries.action: Write an isolated test using one remaining item and two concurrent checkout attempts. Check that stock reservation and order creation commit together; fix the path if both succeed.
entries.acceptance: Exactly one order reserves the last item; the other receives an unavailable response; no negative stock or duplicate payment request is created.

entries.name: Novel Maker
entries.title: Test a complete Novel Maker project backup and recovery
entries.finding: Project data is saved to browser localStorage and an export control already exists.
entries.action: Create a fictional two-chapter project, export it, clear only its disposable test workspace, and restore through the import flow. Add an import path if the existing export has no matching restore.
entries.acceptance: Chapter text, ordering, and project settings survive the round trip; malformed input leaves the current project intact.

entries.name: Pathlight
entries.title: Separate Pathlight demo access from real sign-in
entries.finding: The source has a demo branch that accepts any login credentials when the real backend is unavailable.
entries.action: Make demo access an explicit labelled choice. Require the configured authentication provider for real accounts and show a connection error instead of treating arbitrary credentials as a real login.
entries.acceptance: Invalid credentials never create a real signed-in session; demo state stays separate; a provider outage shows a recoverable error.

entries.name: Help Save
entries.title: Finish the merchant-list failure and retry state
entries.finding: The iOS merchant list error callback contains an unfinished error-message TODO.
entries.action: Implement a visible error state and Retry action in the merchant list. Preserve previously loaded results and prevent repeated retry taps from starting overlapping requests.
entries.acceptance: A forced network failure shows a useful message; Retry reloads results once; the empty state is distinct from an error.

entries.name: Parna
entries.title: Design and implement one server-side plant lookup proxy
entries.finding: The iOS client calls an AI service directly; its README calls for server-side requests before production.
entries.action: Create a narrow plant-name lookup route with input length limits and a server-only provider credential. Change the client service to call this route, using a mock provider in tests.
entries.acceptance: The client binary contains no provider credential; invalid queries fail predictably; the existing plant-detail and fallback views still work.

entries.name: Pasalo
entries.title: Verify Pasalo early-access signup reaches the private admin list
entries.finding: The public early-access API, database persistence, and a separate admin listing are implemented.
entries.action: Run an isolated signup-to-admin test with a fictional address, including consent rejection and duplicate submission. Check the published frontend is pointed at the intended API configuration.
entries.acceptance: One consented signup appears once in the authorized admin list; a duplicate does not create another row; the public API does not disclose the list.

entries.name: Dctor · Development
entries.title: Pin the native Dctor app to one appointment API contract
entries.finding: The development folder contains a native scaffold and several frontend/backend snapshots.
entries.action: Choose and document the canonical appointment endpoint, then add a mocked native API-client test for loading appointments, an expired session, and an empty response.
entries.acceptance: The native app uses one documented base configuration and renders success, signed-out, and empty states without depending on a different source snapshot.

entries.name: Doctor Appointment
entries.title: Replace client-selected appointment identity with a verified session
entries.finding: The prototype server derives the current user from an X-User-Id header or a shared store value.
entries.action: Implement verified session identity for one appointment-read endpoint and ignore caller-supplied user IDs for authorization. Add two-user isolation tests before expanding to the remaining routes.
entries.acceptance: Changing X-User-Id cannot reveal another user’s appointment; missing or expired sessions are rejected; the authenticated user can load their own records.

entries.name: Stria
entries.title: Complete one Stria purchase, restore, and refund sandbox check
entries.finding: StoreKit product mappings and verified entitlements exist; store configuration and sandbox purchase verification remain external release steps.
entries.action: Use a sandbox account and the configured template product to check purchase, relaunch, restore on another test installation, and revoked entitlement handling. Record product IDs and results without credentials.
entries.acceptance: Only the purchased template unlocks; restore recovers it; revoked access is removed; unavailable store products never display invented prices.

entries.name: Lakbay
entries.title: Verify Lakbay membership signup and private CMS access together
entries.finding: The hosted source separates early-access signup from protected CMS and QR administration pages.
entries.action: Write an isolated signup-flow test and an unauthorized-admin test using fictional membership data. Confirm the registration identifier used by the QR view matches the stored signup.
entries.acceptance: A consented signup is visible once to its admin; a logged-out visitor cannot open membership details or the admin QR page.

entries.name: Smart Reminder
entries.title: Test Smart Reminder strict purchase verification failures
entries.finding: The backend supports strict store verification and idempotency by platform and transaction ID.
entries.action: Add an automated test for missing verifier configuration, duplicate transaction submission, and one valid mocked verifier response. Keep production strict mode enabled.
entries.acceptance: Missing configuration grants no entitlement; retries do not duplicate purchases; only a verified transaction changes the subscription state.

entries.name: Sports
entries.title: Persist and restore one sports chat conversation across a restart
entries.finding: The social backend documents in-memory storage intended for local integration work.
entries.action: Add a durable storage adapter for one conversation/message path, with a disposable test database or file. Keep fixture data separate from real conversations.
entries.acceptance: A message and its conversation survive a process restart; repeated message IDs do not duplicate; a failed write does not report success.

entries.name: ÉDIT
entries.title: Add a portable backup for the ÉDIT reading list
entries.finding: Saved reading-list IDs currently live only in localStorage.
entries.action: Add export and import for saved article IDs, validating each ID against the current story catalog. Include a short explanation that saves are device-local.
entries.acceptance: A reading list can be restored in a fresh test browser; unknown IDs are ignored; invalid JSON does not erase the current list.

entries.name: Chainlab
entries.title: Build an isolated signed-transfer proof of concept for Chainlab
entries.finding: The educational chain accepts account names without cryptographic signatures and documents that limitation.
entries.action: Add a small separate signing/verification experiment with generated test keys and replay protection. Document the proposed transaction envelope before changing the existing learning demo.
entries.acceptance: A signature verifies only for the original payload; modified amounts and replayed nonces fail; no real-value or production-security claim is introduced.

entries.name: The Wedding Architect
entries.title: Add an explicit submit-to-Solis action to the wedding brief
entries.finding: The brief builder saves and downloads locally rather than submitting an inquiry.
entries.action: Add an opt-in action that opens or submits the chosen brief through the existing Solis company request flow, preserving the downloadable draft as a fallback.
entries.acceptance: A fictional brief reaches the correct company inbox only after explicit submission and consent; success returns a tracking link; failed submission keeps the draft.

entries.name: Lexi Solis
entries.title: Verify the portfolio contact handoff on phone and desktop
entries.finding: The portfolio is a published static gallery with a correspondence section and an artwork viewer.
entries.action: Check the correspondence action opens the intended inquiry destination, carries the selected work when relevant, and remains reachable by keyboard and on a narrow screen. Fix the destination or control if needed.
entries.acceptance: A visitor can start an inquiry from both layouts; the contact control has a clear accessible label; no form claims delivery without a real handoff.

entries.name: Spido Recipes
entries.title: Verify one Spido premium recipe purchase and restore
entries.finding: Premium recipes are individual StoreKit products, while recipe state uses local storage and backup synchronization.
entries.action: Run one sandbox product purchase and restore with a fictional test account, then check entitlement reconciliation after revocation. Keep recipe progress separate from ownership.
entries.acceptance: Only the purchased recipe unlocks; restore recovers access; revocation removes access without deleting cooking progress.

entries.name: Dctor
entries.title: Add a two-patient appointment access test to Dctor
entries.finding: The hosted patient client connects directly to its dedicated Supabase backend; an older API is retained separately.
entries.action: Use isolated fixtures to test the hosted client’s appointment read and update paths under two patient sessions and a logged-out session. Inspect the corresponding policy definitions.
entries.acceptance: Patient A cannot read or update patient B’s appointment; logged-out requests fail; the legitimate booking flow still succeeds.

entries.name: Aurelia
entries.title: Lock the Aurelia buyer catalog to an explicit public-field contract
entries.finding: The buyer catalog polls a read-only endpoint that is intended to exclude private costs, profit, and owner information.
entries.action: Add a response-contract test covering public availability states and an explicit field allowlist. Test a non-public item and an upstream failure using fixtures.
entries.acceptance: Private cost, profit, owner IDs, and notes never appear; sold/non-public items stay hidden; a failed refresh is clearly reported without exposing private data.

entries.name: Novel Reader
entries.title: Verify Novel Reader edit-log export and recovery end to end
entries.finding: The reader has versioned browser revisions and backup import; hosted reading and local generation have different capabilities.
entries.action: Create a short fictional chapter in a test workspace, export the edit log, import it in a fresh browser, and test a stale-tab edit conflict. Keep private manuscript text out of fixtures.
entries.acceptance: Revisions and pending edits survive the backup round trip; stale writes are rejected; hosted generation controls explain the local-runtime requirement.

entries.name: House of Solis
entries.title: Use the current deployment origin in House of Solis inquiry links
entries.finding: The inquiry script hard-codes an older Site origin for the return URL and product/photo links.
entries.action: Replace fixed-origin construction with the verified current deployment origin or a single validated configuration value. Check inquiry confirmation and product links without sending a real email.
entries.acceptance: The success return and selected-look links resolve to the current Site; the chosen item and size survive the handoff; a fixture submission records no false delivery claim.

entries.name: Pulse
entries.title: Add an authenticated quota boundary for Pulse detector requests
entries.finding: The local detection server is documented as a prototype without user authentication or per-user paid-detector quotas.
entries.action: Protect one detector route with verified identity and a bounded per-user quota. Use a fake detector in tests and keep errors distinct from image verdicts.
entries.acceptance: Anonymous requests are rejected; quota exhaustion makes no provider request; upstream failure produces no authenticity verdict.

entries.name: ScrumHub
entries.title: Define and test one authenticated ScrumHub workspace boundary
entries.finding: The service foundation has domain tokens and versioned state but explicitly lacks account login, tenant membership, and RBAC.
entries.action: Write the minimal identity-to-workspace membership contract, then implement and test it for one gateway read/write route. Do not migrate all domain services in this first slice.
entries.acceptance: A non-member gets 403 on read and write; a valid member reaches only the selected workspace; service tokens remain server-side.

entries.name: Filter
entries.title: Define Filter’s first user problem and clickable flow
entries.finding: The local project contains no implementation source.
entries.action: Write a one-page brief naming the target user, the item being filtered, and one measurable outcome. Sketch three screens and choose the first input/output contract.
entries.acceptance: The brief contains one user job, one primary flow, an explicit out-of-scope list, and a testable first-slice acceptance criterion.
entries.evidence: Project source inventory: no application files found

entries.name: Rover AI
entries.title: Create a reproducible Rover model quality and latency baseline
entries.finding: Rover has a local small transformer and training pipeline; neural chat currently uses the latest prompt without retrieval or conversation memory.
entries.action: Create a held-out set of 20 short prompts, fix model checkpoint and decoding settings, then record output quality, tokens per second, and p50/p95 latency. Keep training examples out of the held-out set.
entries.acceptance: A repeatable command writes checkpoint ID, runtime/hardware, prompts, outputs, and timings; comparison claims are withheld until a matching baseline is measured.

entries.name: Fashion Photography
entries.title: Define the first Fashion Photography offer and shot list
entries.finding: The local project contains no application source or published offer.
entries.action: Choose one service package and target customer, draft a six-image shot list, and define a simple inquiry form with required date, location, and deliverables.
entries.acceptance: A one-page service brief, image-rights checklist, and inquiry-field list are ready for the first portfolio page; no invented client work is presented.
entries.evidence: Project source inventory: no application files found

entries.name: Date Planner
entries.title: Persist one Date Planner event across an app restart
entries.finding: EventData stores a static in-memory list initialized from sample events and mutates it without durable storage.
entries.action: Add a local persistence adapter for create, update, and delete of an event. Use a disposable fixture and load saved records before sample initialization.
entries.acceptance: An added and edited event survives restart; deletion remains deleted; corrupt saved data is preserved and reported rather than silently overwritten.

entries.name: Keepsake
entries.title: Complete Keepsake backup and print checks on a real device
entries.finding: The web app has IndexedDB storage and backup/print controls; its documented browser checks did not verify final native print or backup downloads.
entries.action: Create a fictional album with two test photos, download and restore its backup on another browser, and print one page to PDF at the intended page size.
entries.acceptance: Both photos and captions restore; the PDF page has no clipped text or missing photo; an unavailable-storage error preserves the editor contents.

entries.name: The Cake Architect
entries.title: Connect a cake brief to a real tracked Solis request
entries.finding: The published cake form currently creates and downloads a local brief rather than sending an order request.
entries.action: Add an explicit submit action through the Cake Architect Solis request flow. Include selected cake, servings, date, and delivery needs; use quoted pricing until the merchant confirms terms.
entries.acceptance: A consented fictional request appears in the correct merchant inbox with a tracking link; retries do not duplicate it; failure keeps the local brief.

entries.name: Tara
entries.title: Specify Tara’s first real dispatch boundary and rejection tests
entries.finding: The web and native ride apps simulate drivers, routes, prices, and confirmations; no real driver dispatch exists.
entries.action: Define a request/accept/cancel API contract for a single pilot area and add contract tests with a fake driver adapter. Explicitly separate the simulated UI from a future real dispatch confirmation.
entries.acceptance: A request is never labelled a real confirmed ride without a driver acceptance; cancellation and driver rejection have tested states; the pilot integration checklist names remaining backend dependencies.
